title: Which Rooms Should Have Carpet? A Room-by-Room Guide for Sammamish Homes
meta: Carpet belongs in Sammamish bedrooms, upstairs halls, bonus rooms and stairs, not kitchens, baths or entries. Wills Flooring's room-by-room guide says why.
keywords: which rooms should have carpet, carpet in bedrooms vs hardwood, should stairs be carpeted, carpet in living room or not, carpet installation Sammamish WA, best flooring for each room

blocks.lead: In a Sammamish home, carpet belongs in the bedrooms, the upstairs hallway, the bonus room, the stairs and any finished basement or media room. Keep it out of the kitchen, bathrooms, laundry, mudroom and main entry.
blocks.detail: That split matches how plateau families actually live: hard floors where mud, water and dogs arrive, soft floors where people sleep, play and watch movies. The main-floor living room is the one genuine judgment call, and we cover it below.

blocks.html: Most of the houses we visit in Klahanie, Trossachs and around Pine Lake were built between 1995 and 2012 with builder carpet nearly everywhere except the kitchen. Fifteen years, two kids and a Labrador later, the owners know that layout was wrong, but they are not sure which rooms should keep carpet. This guide goes room by room, explains the reasoning, and flags where the answer depends on your family rather than the floor. For service details, see our carpet installation page.

head: Room
Carpet?
Why, and what to use instead
rows: Warmth underfoot at 6 am, quiet, and a soft landing for kids. A dense nylon or triexta plush or frieze is the standard pick.
It connects carpeted rooms and takes the same foot traffic as the stairs. Use the same carpet as the stairs so the run is continuous.
Carpet grips better than any hard surface for kids and older dogs. It must be a low, dense pile, installed by someone who wraps or caps the nosings tightly.
Cold floor, big open space, toys and screens. Carpet with a thick pad fixes the cold and the echo at once.
Sound absorption and warmth matter most here. A moisture-barrier pad is non-negotiable on any slab.
Open plans that flow into the kitchen want one hard floor throughout. A separate, closed living room can still take carpet.
Chairs, spills and crumbs. Hard flooring plus a rug is easier to live with and to sell.
Water, grease and cleaning chemicals. Vinyl plank or tile.
This is where Sammamish mud and wet dogs land. Nothing soft survives it.
blocks.note: Two-story homes in Sahalee and Beaver Lake often end up with a clean rule: hard floors downstairs, carpet upstairs. It is simple to explain to a buyer and it works.

blocks.text: Why bedrooms and the upstairs still want carpet in 2026

items.title: Warmth where you are barefoot
items.text: Sammamish bedrooms sit over garages, crawlspaces or open ceilings below, and the plateau runs a few degrees colder than Seattle. Carpet and pad insulate better than any hard floor, which is what people notice when they switch a bedroom to plank and regret it by November.

items.title: Quiet between floors
items.text: Carpet upstairs is the biggest thing keeping footsteps, dropped toys and early-morning dog nails from reaching the main floor. Families who put hard flooring in upstairs bedrooms almost always add rugs back within a year, which costs more and looks less finished.

items.title: Soft landings
items.text: Toddlers, kids wrestling on the floor and older relatives all fall more safely on carpet. Stairs are the clearest case: a carpeted stair with a dense pile is the safest stair in the house, especially for dogs whose nails cannot grip a hard tread.

items.title: The budget goes further upstairs
items.text: Bedrooms are large, low-traffic rooms that do not need premium flooring to look good. Carpet there, with the hard-surface budget saved for the main floor where buyers and guests actually look, is how most Sammamish remodels come out looking finished.

blocks.text: Stairs, bonus rooms and basements: the judgment calls

items.text: Carpet is the right answer for most Sammamish families, but only in a low, dense cut pile or a tight loop. Thick plush over a nosing wears through at the edge within a few years. If the staircase is a showpiece visible from the entry, hardwood treads with a carpet runner give you looks and grip.
items.note: Ask for the nosing to be wrapped, not capped loosely, and for a firm pad on the treads

items.text: The room over the garage in a Klahanie or Trossachs two-story is the coldest room in the house. Carpet with a thicker, denser pad solves that and makes the room usable as a playroom or teen space.
items.note: If the room doubles as a home gym, consider carpet tiles so a damaged section can be swapped

items.text: Carpet wins for sound and comfort, but only after the slab passes a moisture test. Carpet over a damp slab is the most common flooring failure we see on the plateau.
items.note: Use a pad with a built-in moisture barrier and keep a dehumidifier in the plan

blocks.text: Rooms where carpet is a mistake in a Sammamish house

a.title: Keep or install carpet when
items: The room is a bedroom, upstairs hall, stair run or bonus room
You want the floor to be warm and quiet more than you want it to be washable
Kids or older dogs use the space daily
The subfloor is wood or a slab that tests dry

b.title: Skip carpet when
items: The room opens directly to the kitchen in one continuous space
Wet dogs, boots and bikes come through the door
There is any history of a slab leak, flooding or a damp crawlspace
Someone in the house has severe dust allergies and will not vacuum weekly

blocks.title: The open-plan trap:
blocks.text: Many 2000s plateau homes have a family room that flows into the kitchen with no doorway. Carpeting it puts a soft edge two steps from the stove and the dog bowl: it stains first and sells worst. In an open plan, run one hard floor through the whole space and put comfort back with a large rug.
Mistakes we see on the plateau

items.html: Carpeting everything because the builder did. Builder-grade carpet in a dining room or main entry was a cost decision, not a design one. Do not repeat it.

Ripping carpet out of every upstairs bedroom to modernize. Cold, echoing bedrooms are the most common regret we hear at follow-up visits. Kids' rooms and the primary bedroom almost always want carpet.
Ignoring the pad. A dense, thinner pad on stairs and a thicker pad in bedrooms is the right pairing. One pad for the whole house is how stairs get spongy and bedrooms feel thin.

Carpeting a basement without a moisture test. Sammamish sits on clay and glacial till. Even a finished basement that has looked dry for years can wick moisture through a slab. Read our basement carpet guide before you commit.

blocks.text: Checklist before you decide room by room

items.html: Walk the house with the daily routine in mind. Where do wet dogs, sports bags and groceries enter? Those rooms go hard-surface.
Draw the main-floor sightlines. Any rooms visible from each other without a door should share one floor. Closed rooms can differ.
Match fiber to the room. Nylon or triexta on stairs and halls, softer polyester or triexta in low-traffic bedrooms. Our fiber guide explains the trade-offs.
Test any slab and check the crawlspace. We meter subfloors at the free estimate, and a reading that is too high changes the plan for that room.
Think about the next owner. Sammamish buyers expect hard floors on the main level and are happy with good carpet upstairs. Match that and the house shows well.

faq.q: Should bedrooms have carpet or hardwood?
faq.a: For most Sammamish families, carpet. Bedrooms are where warmth, quiet and a soft floor matter most and where spills and mud matter least. Hardwood or vinyl plank in bedrooms looks clean in photos but usually ends up under rugs within a year, especially over a garage or crawlspace.

faq.q: Is it better to carpet stairs or leave them hardwood?
faq.a: Carpet grips better and is safer for kids, older adults and dogs. If the staircase is a feature you can see from the front door, hardwood treads with a carpet runner give you the look plus the grip. Either way, keep the pile low and dense so the nosings do not wear through.

faq.q: Can I carpet the living room if it opens to the kitchen?
faq.a: We advise against it. An open plan reads as one room, and a carpet edge two steps from the stove stains first and looks chopped up to buyers. Run a hard floor through the whole connected space and add a large rug for comfort where the sofa sits.

faq.q: Is carpet in a basement a bad idea in Sammamish?
faq.a: Not if the slab tests dry and you use a pad with a moisture barrier. The plateau's clay soils mean many basements carry moisture through the concrete even when they look dry. We meter the slab at the estimate; if it fails, vinyl plank is the safer choice for that room.

faq.q: Does carpet hurt resale value in Sammamish?
faq.a: Only where buyers expect hard floors: kitchen, entry, dining and an open main living area. Good-condition carpet in bedrooms, halls, bonus rooms and stairs is what most Sammamish buyers expect and is not a negative. Worn or stained carpet anywhere is.
